docs.title: Hrefc
docs.text:
Point at a link and a small card fades in above it, centred over the link, with a connector arrow. The card shows the target page's title and a line about it. Move the pointer away and the card disappears.

vexy-hrefc is a client-side link-preview library in one file, with no runtime dependencies. It reads Open Graph tags first and falls back to plainer HTML. When the browser blocks a cross-origin request, it routes the request through a reader proxy instead. Failures are silent by design: if a preview cannot be built, nothing appears.

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-hrefc/dist/hrefc.global.min.js"></script>
<a class="hrefc" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperlink">hyperlink</a>
<script>
  Hrefc();
</script>

That is a working preview. See it run in the basic demo.

docs.title: What happens when you hover a link
docs.text:
1. You call Hrefc() (or hrefc() from the ESM build). It finds every link that matches [data-hrefc], a.hrefc and attaches pointer and focus listeners.
  2. You hover a link for 120 ms (hoverDelay). The library resolves the link's href to an absolute URL.
  3. It fetches the target page's HTML. Same-origin links use the browser's fetch. Cross-origin links go through the proxy chain, which is r.jina.ai by default.
  4. It parses the HTML and extracts a title, a description, and optionally an image and a favicon.
  5. If at least a title, description or image was found, the card is filled and fades in. Otherwise nothing is shown.
  6. The result is cached per URL, so the next hover over the same link shows the card without a network request.

How it works covers each step in detail.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text: The first version lived inside a Webflow page and used Tippy.js and Popper loaded from a CDN. It worked until a link pointed to another site and CORS blocked the fetch. This rewrite drops both libraries in favour of its own positioning code, adds a proxy fallback so cross-origin links preview, and makes the card restyleable without editing the source.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• One file, no dependencies. A single <script> tag, or an import.
  • Silent failures. No "Loading…" text and no error text. The card appears when it is ready, or not at all.
  • Cross-origin support. Cross-origin links route through a pluggable reader proxy.
  • Title, description, thumbnail, favicon. Each one can be switched on or off. Title and description are on by default; thumbnail and favicon are opt-in.
  • Restyleable. The card inherits the page's font and colour, follows the system dark or light setting, and accepts CSS variables or a fully custom render() function.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Getting started: install the library and show a first preview.
  • Configuration: every option and its default.
  • Styling: CSS variables, classes and custom markup.
  • Examples: the live demo pages, simplest first.

Note

vexy-hrefc is a reading aid, not load-bearing infrastructure. When a page will not cooperate, the preview stays out of the way.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: The public surface: three ways to create an instance, five instance methods, and a few exports. Type definitions ship as dist/hrefc.d.ts.

docs.title: hrefc(config?) → Hrefc
docs.text:
Creates a running instance and scans the document. hrefc.init is an alias.

import { hrefc } from 'vexy-hrefc';

const inst = hrefc({ selector: 'a.preview' });

docs.title: new Hrefc(config?) → Hrefc
docs.text:
The class behind hrefc(). hrefc(config) returns new Hrefc(config).

import { Hrefc } from 'vexy-hrefc';

const inst = new Hrefc({ trigger: 'click' });

docs.title: auto() → Hrefc
docs.text:
Creates an instance from window.HrefcConfig, or from the defaults when that is not set. Intended for script-tag use.

<script>
  window.HrefcConfig = { content: { thumbnail: true } };
</script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-hrefc/dist/hrefc.global.min.js"></script>
<script>
  Hrefc.auto();
</script>

docs.title: Instance properties and methods
Exports
docs.text:
Named ES module exports. The default export is hrefc.

Export Type Contents hrefc function Create an instance. auto function Create an instance from window.HrefcConfig. Hrefc class The instance class. defaults object The default configuration. proxies object Built-in proxy adapters jina, allorigins, corsproxy. thumbnailProviders object Built-in thumbnail providers ogimage, mshots, microlink. 
import { hrefc, defaults, proxies, thumbnailProviders, Hrefc } from 'vexy-hrefc';

hrefc({ fetch: { proxies: [proxies.allorigins, proxies.corsproxy] } });

docs.title: Global and ESM names
docs.text:
The global build sets window.Hrefc to the hrefc function and copies the named exports onto it.

ESM Global Notes hrefc() Hrefc() The global Hrefc is the function. hrefc.init Hrefc.init Alias. auto() Hrefc.auto() Reads window.HrefcConfig. defaults Hrefc.defaults Default configuration. proxies Hrefc.proxies Proxy adapters. thumbnailProviders Hrefc.thumbnails or Hrefc.thumbnailProviders Thumbnail providers. Hrefc Hrefc.Hrefc The class.

docs.title: PreviewData
docs.text:
The object extracted from a target page and passed to render, onShow and thumbnail providers.

Field Type Contents url string The page URL. title string Page title, from Open Graph, Twitter card or <title>. description string Description from meta tags, or trimmed body text. image string Absolute image URL, or ''. Filled only when content.thumbnail is on. favicon string Absolute favicon URL, or ''. Filled only when content.favicon is on.

docs.title: render(data, link)
docs.text:
Replaces the card's contents. Return a DOM Node to insert it directly. Any other value is converted to a string and set as innerHTML; null and undefined give an empty card.

hrefc({
  render: (data, link) => {
    const el = document.createElement('div');
    el.textContent = data.title;
    return el;
  },
});

Warning

A returned string is set as innerHTML. Escape any field you do not control.

docs.title: Hooks
Adapter signatures
docs.text:
type ProxyAdapter = (url: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<string>;
type ThumbnailProvider = (url: string, data: PreviewData, opts: ThumbnailConfig) => string | null;

A ProxyAdapter resolves with the target's HTML or throws to pass to the next adapter. A ThumbnailProvider returns an image URL or null to pass to the next provider. See Fetching and CORS and Thumbnails.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All options live in one object passed to hrefc(config), new Hrefc(config) or window.HrefcConfig. Pass only the options you want to change; the rest keep their defaults.

const inst = hrefc({
  trigger: 'hover',
  content: { thumbnail: true },
  popup: { theme: 'dark' },
});

docs.title: How your options are merged
docs.text:
Your object is deep-merged onto the defaults by mergeConfig():

  • Nested plain objects merge key by key. content: { thumbnail: true } changes one flag and leaves title, description and the other content keys at their defaults.
  • Arrays and scalar values replace the default. Passing fetch.proxies: ['allorigins'] gives you a chain of exactly one proxy; it does not append to the default chain.

The defaults object itself is never modified. You can read it as defaults (ESM) or Hrefc.defaults (global).

docs.title: Top-level options
docs.text:
Option Default Effect selector '[data-hrefc], a.hrefc' CSS selector for the links that get previews. trigger 'hover' What opens a preview: 'hover', 'click' or 'manual'. hoverDelay 120 Milliseconds the pointer must rest on a link before the fetch starts. hideDelay 160 Milliseconds after the pointer leaves before the card hides.

The three triggers attach different listeners:

  • 'hover' listens for pointerenter, pointerleave, focus and blur, so keyboard focus also opens a preview.
  • 'click' listens for click, prevents the default navigation, and shows the preview.
  • 'manual' attaches no listeners. Open previews from your own code with inst.show(link).
hrefc({ trigger: 'click', hideDelay: 300 });

docs.title: content
docs.text:
What goes on the card, and how text is trimmed.

Option Default Effect title true Show the page title. description true Show the description line. thumbnail false Extract an image and show a thumbnail. See Thumbnails. favicon false Show the site's favicon next to the title. cta null Footer text below the description, for example 'Click to read more'. HTML is allowed. Rendered with the class hrefc-cta. descriptionMaxLength 350 Maximum length of a description taken from the page body text. stripTitleSuffix false Cut the title at the first separator, so "Refunds \| Acme Help" becomes "Refunds". titleSeparators ['\|', '–', '—', '·', '»', '::'] Separators checked, in order, when stripTitleSuffix is on.

descriptionMaxLength applies only to the body-text fallback. A description taken from a <meta> tag is used as written. When the body text is longer than the limit, it is cut and an ellipsis (…) is appended.

stripTitleSuffix checks the separators in the order listed and cuts at the first one found after the first character. Title "Docs · Getting started | Acme" with the default list becomes "Docs · Getting started", because | is checked before ·.

hrefc({
  content: { favicon: true, stripTitleSuffix: true, cta: 'Click to read more →' },
});

docs.title: fetch
docs.text:
How the target page's HTML is fetched. See Fetching and CORS for the full picture.

Option Default Effect timeout 6500 Milliseconds before a single fetch attempt is aborted. sameOriginDirect true Use the browser's fetch for same-origin links. crossOriginStrategy 'proxy' 'proxy' sends cross-origin links straight to the proxy chain. 'native-first' tries the browser's fetch first. proxies [jina] Ordered proxy chain. Entries are names ('jina', 'allorigins', 'corsproxy') or adapter functions. 
hrefc({
  fetch: { timeout: 4000, proxies: ['jina', 'allorigins'] },
});

docs.title: thumbnail
docs.text:
Where images come from when content.thumbnail is true.

Option Default Effect width 480 Width passed to the mshots screenshot service, in pixels. providers ['ogimage', 'mshots', 'microlink'] Ordered list of image providers. Names or functions. iframe true Fall back to a scaled, sandboxed <iframe> of the page when no image can be shown. iframeViewport { width: 1280, height: 800 } Size at which the fallback iframe renders the page before it is scaled down. 
hrefc({
  content: { thumbnail: true },
  thumbnail: { providers: ['ogimage'], iframe: false },
});

docs.title: cache
docs.text:
Extracted preview data is kept in memory per URL.

Option Default Effect enabled true Cache extracted data. max 200 Maximum number of entries. Adding one more evicts the least recently stored entry. 
hrefc({ cache: { max: 50 } });

docs.title: popup
docs.text:
The card: size, placement, theme and behaviour.

Option Default Effect maxWidth 360 Maximum card width, in pixels. offset 12 Gap between the link and the card, in pixels. placement 'auto' 'auto' places the card above the link and flips it below only when there is no room above. 'top' and 'bottom' force a side. arrow true Show the connector arrow that points from the card to the link. classPrefix 'hrefc' Prefix for every generated class name. appendTo null Element (or function returning an element) the card is mounted in. null means document.body. inheritFont true Use the page's font. When false, the card uses a system UI font stack. theme 'auto' 'auto' follows the system colour scheme. 'light' or 'dark' pins it. injectStyles true Insert the default stylesheet into <head>. interactive true Moving the pointer onto the card keeps it open, and clicking the card follows the link. zIndex 9999 Stacking order of the card.

In every placement, the card is centred horizontally over the link and then clamped so it stays at least 8 px inside the viewport.

hrefc({
  popup: { maxWidth: 420, placement: 'top', theme: 'dark', offset: 8 },
});

Class names, CSS variables and themes are covered in Styling.

docs.title: classes
docs.text:
Override individual generated class names. Empty by default. The keys are:

popup, card, arrow, head, favicon, title, desc, cta, thumb, thumbWide, thumbHalf, thumbFloat, frame.

hrefc({ classes: { card: 'card', title: 'card__title', desc: 'card__body' } });

Note

The default stylesheet uses classPrefix and does not know about names set in classes. Parts you rename this way need your own CSS.

docs.title: render
docs.text:
Replace the card's contents. render(data, link) receives the extracted data and the link element.

  • If it returns a DOM Node, that node is placed in the card.
  • Otherwise the return value is converted to a string and set as the innerHTML of a wrapper <div>. null or undefined give an empty card.
hrefc({
  render: (data, link) => {
    const el = document.createElement('strong');
    el.textContent = data.title;
    return el;
  },
});

Warning

A returned string is set as innerHTML. Escape any field you do not control.

The data object has the fields url, title, description, image and favicon. See the API reference.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Callbacks for the preview lifecycle. All default to null.

Option Signature Called when onShow (data, link, popupEl) => void A card was shown. onHide (link) => void The card was hidden after the pointer left. onError (error, link) => void A fetch failed, or the page had no title, description or image. 
hrefc({
  onShow: (data) => console.log('previewed', data.url),
  onError: (err, link) => console.warn('no preview for', link.href, err),
});

An exception thrown inside a hook is caught and ignored, so a broken hook cannot break the page.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: How to build the library, run the tests, build this documentation site and release a new version.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Node.js with npm (on some machines npm is a pnpm shim; the scripts use only commands both accept).
  • For the documentation site: uv, which provides uvx.
  • For releases: an npm account with publish rights to vexy-hrefc.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Contents src/ Library source, one ES module per concern, plus hrefc.d.ts. test/ Tests for node --test. scripts/build.mjs The esbuild bundling script. dist/ Build output. Not committed. src_docs/md/ This documentation, plus the demo pages and their assets. src_docs/mkdocs.yml Documentation site configuration. docs/ The generated site that GitHub Pages serves. Do not edit by hand.

docs.title: Build the library
docs.text:
1. Install the development dependencies (esbuild, linkedom):

    npm install

  2. Run the build:

    npm run build

scripts/build.mjs bundles src/index.js with esbuild, targeting ES2019, into:

  • dist/hrefc.esm.js: ES module.
  • dist/hrefc.global.js: IIFE that sets window.Hrefc.
  • dist/hrefc.global.min.js: minified IIFE.
  • dist/hrefc.css: the default stylesheet from src/styles.js, prefix hrefc.
  • dist/hrefc.d.ts: copied from src/hrefc.d.ts.

It also copies hrefc.global.min.js and hrefc.css into src_docs/md/assets/, so the demo pages use the bundle you just built. It prints the size of each output file.

./build.sh lib runs npm install and npm run build in one step; ./build.sh with no argument builds the library and then the documentation. npm run clean removes dist/.

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
npm test

This runs node --test. The tests cover configuration merging, metadata extraction and the fetcher. Extraction tests use linkedom to provide a DOM in Node, so run npm install first.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
ProperDocs builds the site from src_docs/md/ into docs/ using fly-january 0.4.0 or later (remote theme assets). The site configuration sets extra.fly.chrome to none.

  1. Build once, in strict mode:

    ./build.sh docs

    or, equivalently, src_docs/build.sh.

  2. Or preview with live reload on http://127.0.0.1:8000:

    src_docs/build.sh serve

The build replaces the contents of docs/ and adds docs/.nojekyll. Files in src_docs/md/demos/ and src_docs/md/assets/ are copied to the site unchanged.

On every push to main that changes src_docs/, the Docs GitHub workflow runs src_docs/build.sh and commits the rebuilt docs/ folder.

Tip

Run npm run build before building the docs when the library has changed, so the demos pick up the new bundle in src_docs/md/assets/.

docs.title: Release to npm
docs.text:
./publish.sh performs the whole release:

  1. Checks that you are logged in to npm (npm whoami) and offers npm login when run interactively.
  2. Runs npm install, npm test and npm run build.
  3. Runs uvx gitnextver@latest, which commits pending changes, tags the next vX.Y.Z and pushes.
  4. Writes the new version into package.json, commits and pushes that change.
  5. Runs npm publish --access public.

If gitnextver creates no new tag, the script publishes the version already in package.json.

docs.title: Code conventions
docs.text:
• No runtime dependencies.
  • Each source file starts with a this_file comment that records its path.
  • Failures are silent in the UI; errors are reported only through onError.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Live demo pages, simplest first. Each page shows a working preview, the code that produced it, and a Copy button for that code. The demos load the bundle from assets/hrefc.global.min.js on this site.

Open the demo index to browse them, or jump straight to one:

Demo What it shows 01 – The one-liner A link, a class and one function call. 02 – Content toggles Title, description and favicon. 03 – Thumbnails og:image, screenshots and the iframe fallback. 04 – Styling CSS variables, dark mode and a full reskin. 05 – Custom render Your own card markup through render(). 06 – Proxies and CORS A custom fetch chain.

docs.title: 05 – Custom render
docs.text:
The other demos are embedded on the pages that explain them: Configuration, Thumbnails, Styling and Fetching and CORS.

Note

The previews in these demos fetch live pages through public proxies. If a proxy is slow or rate-limited, a preview may not appear; that is the silent-failure behaviour working as designed.

docs.title: Fetching and CORS
docs.text: To build a preview, vexy-hrefc must read the target page's HTML. For links on your own site, the browser allows it. For links to other sites, the browser usually refuses: that is CORS (cross-origin resource sharing), and JavaScript on your page cannot override it. Cross-origin links therefore go through a reader proxy, a service that fetches the page on its server and returns the HTML with headers the browser accepts.

docs.title: Which route a link takes
docs.text:
For each link, the fetcher builds an ordered list of attempts:

  1. Native fetch, included only when:
    • the link is same-origin and fetch.sameOriginDirect is true (default), or
    • the link is cross-origin and fetch.crossOriginStrategy is 'native-first'.
  2. Each proxy in fetch.proxies, in order.

The attempts run one after another. The first one that returns HTML wins. Each attempt gets its own fetch.timeout (6500 ms by default); when it expires, the request is aborted through its AbortSignal and the next attempt starts. If every attempt fails, the preview stays hidden and onError is called.

Native requests are sent with credentials: 'omit', so cookies are not included.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
You hover https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperlink on https://example.com with the default configuration:

  1. The link is cross-origin and the strategy is 'proxy', so no native attempt is made.
  2. The jina adapter requests https://r.jina.ai/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperlink.
  3. The response HTML is parsed, and the og:title and og:description become the card text.
  4. The result is cached under the link's absolute URL.

docs.title: The default proxy
docs.text:
The default chain contains one proxy, jina, which uses r.jina.ai. The adapter is the JavaScript equivalent of:

curl "https://r.jina.ai/https://example.com/" \
  -H "X-Engine: direct" \
  -H "X-Return-Format: html"

It needs no API key.

docs.title: Native first
docs.text:
Set fetch.crossOriginStrategy to 'native-first' if the sites you link to send permissive CORS headers. A direct request is faster and skips the proxy; when it fails, the proxy chain still runs.

hrefc({
  fetch: { crossOriginStrategy: 'native-first' },
});

docs.title: Add and reorder proxies
docs.text:
Three proxies are built in. Refer to them by name:

Name Request sent 'jina' https://r.jina.ai/<url> with X-Engine: direct and X-Return-Format: html 'allorigins' https://api.allorigins.win/raw?url=<encoded url> 'corsproxy' https://corsproxy.io/?url=<encoded url> 
hrefc({
  fetch: { proxies: ['jina', 'allorigins', 'corsproxy'] },
});

Order is priority. Because arrays replace rather than merge, this list is the whole chain. Unknown names are dropped.

docs.title: Write your own adapter
docs.text:
An adapter is an async function (url, signal) => Promise<string>. Resolve with the page's HTML to stop the chain; throw to pass to the next adapter.

async function myProxy(url, signal) {
  const res = await fetch('https://my-reader.example/?u=' + encodeURIComponent(url), { signal });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error('myProxy ' + res.status); // try the next adapter
  return res.text(); // HTML: the chain stops here
}

hrefc({
  fetch: { proxies: [myProxy, 'jina'] },
});

Pass the signal to your fetch call so the timeout can cancel it. Names and functions can be mixed in one list. The built-in adapters are also exported as proxies.jina, proxies.allorigins and proxies.corsproxy.

docs.title: Caching and de-duplication
docs.text:
• Cache. With cache.enabled (default true), extracted data is stored per URL, up to cache.max entries (default 200). A second hover over the same link shows the card without a network request.
  • In-flight de-duplication. If you hover the same link several times before the first fetch finishes, all hovers share one request.
  • Empty results. A page with no title, no description and no image counts as a failure. It is not cached, so a later hover tries again.
hrefc({
  fetch: { timeout: 4000 },
  cache: { max: 50 },
});

Warning

The built-in proxies are free public services. They can rate-limit, go offline or change behaviour without notice. Keep a fallback in the chain, or put your own reader first.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This page shows how to load vexy-hrefc, mark the links you want previewed, and start it.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A web page you can edit.
  • For the npm route: Node.js and a bundler or framework that understands ES modules.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Choose the method that matches how you build the page.

Script tagnpm

No build step. The script defines a global Hrefc on window.

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-hrefc/dist/hrefc.global.min.js"></script>

The same file is also on unpkg: https://unpkg.com/vexy-hrefc/dist/hrefc.global.min.js.

npm install vexy-hrefc

import { hrefc } from 'vexy-hrefc';

The npm package contains these files in dist/:

File Format hrefc.esm.js ES module (the package entry point) hrefc.global.js Readable IIFE that sets window.Hrefc hrefc.global.min.js Minified IIFE that sets window.Hrefc hrefc.css The default stylesheet, standalone hrefc.d.ts TypeScript type definitions

docs.title: Show your first preview
docs.text:
1. Load the script as shown above.

  2. Add class="hrefc" to a link:

    <a class="hrefc" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperlink">hyperlink</a>

  3. Start the library after the script has loaded:

    <script>
  Hrefc();
</script>

  4. Hover the link.

A card fades in above the link, centred over it, with a small arrow pointing down at the link. It shows the page title and a description. Move the pointer away and the card fades out.

docs.title: Use it from an ES module
docs.text:
hrefc(config) creates and returns a running instance:

import { hrefc } from 'vexy-hrefc';

const inst = hrefc({ selector: 'a.preview' });

The stylesheet is injected automatically. To ship it yourself, for example after setting popup.injectStyles to false, import the standalone file once:

import 'vexy-hrefc/css';

docs.title: Configure from a script tag without arguments
docs.text:
If you cannot pass arguments, set window.HrefcConfig before the library starts and call Hrefc.auto():

<script>
  window.HrefcConfig = { content: { thumbnail: true } };
</script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-hrefc/dist/hrefc.global.min.js"></script>
<script>
  Hrefc.auto();
</script>

auto() reads window.HrefcConfig and falls back to the defaults when it is not set.

docs.title: Why not every link previews
docs.text:
The default selector is [data-hrefc], a.hrefc. A link previews only if it has class="hrefc" or a data-hrefc attribute. This keeps cards from appearing on navigation links, footer links and in-page anchors.

To preview more links, pass your own selector. For example, every absolute http or https link inside <main>:

hrefc({ selector: 'main a[href^="http"]' });

Tip

The selector is passed to querySelectorAll. Any selector that querySelectorAll accepts works.

docs.title: Links added after start-up
docs.text:
hrefc() scans the document once, when it starts. Links inserted later (a loaded comment thread, a router view, search results) are not wired up until you call refresh():

const inst = hrefc();

// later, after inserting links into the page:
inst.refresh();

For a single known element, inst.add(el) attaches without rescanning. Links that are already attached are skipped, so calling refresh() twice does not add duplicate listeners. See the API reference for every instance method.

Note

If a page blocks the request and every proxy fails, nothing appears: no spinner and no error message. To see why a preview failed, use the onError hook described in Configuration.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
This page follows one hover from the pointer event to the visible card, module by module. The source lives in src/.

Module Responsibility index.js The Hrefc class: link discovery, event listeners, timers, hooks. config.js The defaults object and the deep merge (mergeConfig, resolveConfig). fetcher.js Fetch attempts, timeouts, the LRU cache, in-flight de-duplication. proxies.js The built-in proxy adapters jina, allorigins, corsproxy. extract.js HTML parsing and metadata extraction. thumbnail.js The thumbnail provider chain ogimage, mshots, microlink. popup.js The single popup element: content, positioning, show and hide. styles.js The default stylesheet and its one-time injection. util.js URL helpers and withTimeout.

docs.title: 1. Start-up
docs.text:
hrefc(config) calls new Hrefc(config). The constructor:

  1. Merges your options onto defaults.
  2. Creates one fetcher and one popup for the instance. The popup injects the default stylesheet into <head> once per class prefix, unless popup.injectStyles is false.
  3. Runs refresh(), which calls document.querySelectorAll(selector) and attaches listeners to each match. Attached links are tracked in a WeakSet, so a link is never attached twice.
  4. Adds passive scroll and resize listeners on window that re-position a visible card.

docs.title: 2. Hover intent
docs.text:
With trigger: 'hover', pointerenter or focus on a link records it as the desired link and starts a hoverDelay timer (120 ms). Leaving the link (pointerleave or blur) clears the desired link, cancels the timer, and starts a hideDelay timer (160 ms).

When the hover timer fires, the instance resolves the href against location.href. Links with no href, or an href that cannot be parsed as a URL, are ignored.

docs.title: 3. Fetch
docs.text:
fetcher.getData(url) returns a promise of preview data:

  1. A cached result is returned immediately.
  2. A request already in flight for the same URL is shared.
  3. Otherwise the attempt list runs: native fetch (when allowed), then each proxy. Each attempt is wrapped in withTimeout, which aborts it through an AbortController after fetch.timeout ms.

Details are on the Fetching and CORS page.

docs.title: 4. Extraction
docs.text:
The HTML is parsed with DOMParser and extractMeta() fills a PreviewData object:

Field Sources, in order title og:title, twitter:title, <title>. Optional suffix stripping. description og:description, twitter:description, meta name="description", then the body text with script, style, noscript, template and svg removed, cut to descriptionMaxLength. Skipped when content.description is false. image og:image, og:image:url, twitter:image, twitter:image:src. Only when content.thumbnail is on. Made absolute. favicon Largest <link rel="…icon…">, else /favicon.ico. Only when content.favicon is on. Made absolute. url The response URL for native fetches (after redirects), or the requested URL for proxies.

If title, description and image are all empty, the result is rejected as "nothing worth showing" and not cached.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Given this target HTML:

<html>
  <head>
    <title>Refunds | Acme Help</title>
    <meta name="description" content="How to get your money back.">
  </head>
  <body>…</body>
</html>

With content: { stripTitleSuffix: true }, the extracted data is:

{
  url: 'https://help.acme.example/refunds',
  title: 'Refunds',
  description: 'How to get your money back.',
  image: '',
  favicon: '',
}

docs.title: 5. Showing the card
docs.text:
When the data arrives, the instance checks that the link is still the desired one. If you have already moved to another link, the stale result is dropped. Click triggers and show() calls skip this check.

The popup then:

  1. Creates its element on first use and appends it to popup.appendTo (default document.body). One element is reused for every link.
  2. Fills the card from render() or from the default layout.
  3. Measures the link and the card, picks a side (above unless there is no room), centres the card over the link, and clamps it 8 px inside the viewport.
  4. Points the arrow at the link's horizontal centre.
  5. On the next animation frame, positions again and sets data-show="1", which triggers the CSS fade-in.

onShow(data, link, popupEl) is then called.

docs.title: 6. Hiding
docs.text: When the hide timer fires and the pointer is not over the card, data-show is removed and onHide(link) is called. With popup.interactive on, entering the card cancels the hide timer, and leaving it starts the timer again. Clicking the card navigates to the link's href, unless the click landed on a link or button inside the card.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text: Any error in fetching or extraction ends the promise chain quietly: no card appears, and onError(error, link) is called. Errors thrown by hooks are caught and ignored.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text: Short answers to common setups. Each recipe is a problem and a code block.

docs.title: Add it to a Webflow site
docs.text:
No build step is needed.

  1. In Webflow, open Project Settings → Custom Code → Footer Code.

  2. Paste:

    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-hrefc/dist/hrefc.global.min.js"></script>
<script>
  Hrefc();
</script>

  3. In the Designer, give each link you want previewed the class hrefc.

  4. Publish the site.

Hovering a link with the class hrefc now shows a card.

docs.title: Strip the site name from titles
docs.text:
Help and documentation pages often have titles like "Refunds | Acme Help". Cut the suffix so the card reads "Refunds":

hrefc({ content: { stripTitleSuffix: true } });

docs.title: Preview footnotes and citations
docs.text:
Show where footnotes and citations point without scrolling to the bottom:

hrefc({ selector: 'a.footnote-ref, sup a, cite a' });

docs.title: Click instead of hover
docs.text:
Better on touch screens, and for readers who do not want cards following the pointer:

hrefc({ trigger: 'click' });

The click opens the preview instead of navigating. With popup.interactive on (the default), clicking the card follows the link.

docs.title: Open previews from your own code
docs.text:
Switch off automatic triggers and call show():

const inst = hrefc({ trigger: 'manual' });

document.querySelector('#preview-btn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  inst.show(document.querySelector('#target-link'));
});

docs.title: Show the hostname in a custom card
docs.text:
const esc = (s) => s.replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => `&#${c.charCodeAt(0)};`);

hrefc({
  render: (data) => `
    <strong class="card-title">${esc(data.title)}</strong>
    <small class="card-url">${esc(new URL(data.url).hostname)}</small>
    <p>${esc(data.description)}</p>
  `,
});

The esc helper escapes the page's text before it goes into innerHTML.

docs.title: Pick up links added later
docs.text:
hrefc() scans once at start-up. After inserting links (a router view, infinite scroll, a comment thread), rescan:

const inst = hrefc();

// after adding links to the DOM:
inst.refresh();

To rescan only part of the page, pass a root element: inst.refresh(container).

docs.title: Log failures without showing them
docs.text:
The card never shows errors. To find out why a preview did not appear, use onError:

hrefc({
  onError: (err, link) => console.warn('no preview for', link.href, err),
});

docs.title: Mount the card inside a dialog
docs.text:
If your links sit in a modal that traps stacking or focus, mount the card there:

hrefc({ popup: { appendTo: () => document.querySelector('dialog[open]') } });

When the function returns nothing, the card is mounted in document.body.

docs.title: Avoid class-name collisions
docs.text:
If hrefc- clashes with existing CSS, change the prefix:

hrefc({ popup: { classPrefix: 'lp' } });

The injected stylesheet follows the new prefix.

docs.title: Styling
docs.text: The card ships with a default look that inherits your page's font and colour. To change it, you have three levels, each with more reach than the last: set CSS variables, write CSS against the class names, or replace the markup with render().

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
The default card is built from these elements:

div.hrefc-popup          positioning, fade, theme variables
├── div.hrefc-arrow      connector arrow (when popup.arrow is true)
└── div.hrefc-card       the visible box
    ├── img.hrefc-thumb  or div.hrefc-thumb-frame (when content.thumbnail is true)
    ├── div.hrefc-head
    │   ├── img.hrefc-favicon (when content.favicon is true)
    │   └── span.hrefc-title
    ├── p.hrefc-desc
    └── div.hrefc-cta    (when content.cta is set)

.hrefc-popup holds the --hrefc-* variables. Both the card and the arrow read them, so the arrow follows the card's --hrefc-bg and --hrefc-border automatically. Remove the arrow with popup: { arrow: false }.

The popup also carries state attributes you can target:

Attribute Values Meaning data-show "1" or absent Present while the card is visible. data-placement "top", "bottom" Which side of the link the card is on. data-theme "light", "dark" or absent Set when popup.theme is not 'auto'.

Note

The default stylesheet is inserted as the first child of <head>. Any CSS your page loads later wins without !important.

docs.title: Level 1: CSS variables
docs.text:
For a quick reskin, override the variables on .hrefc-popup.

Variable Default (light) Controls --hrefc-fg #1a1a1a Text colour --hrefc-bg #fff Card and arrow background --hrefc-border rgba(0,0,0,.12) Border colour --hrefc-radius 12px Corner radius --hrefc-shadow 0 8px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.16) Drop shadow --hrefc-desc rgba(0,0,0,.66) Description colour --hrefc-thumb-bg rgba(0,0,0,.04) Thumbnail placeholder background --hrefc-pad 12px 14px (fallback) Inner padding --hrefc-size 14px (fallback) Base font size --hrefc-title inherit (fallback) Title colour --hrefc-cta inherit (fallback) Call-to-action colour

The last four are not set by the stylesheet; it reads them with the fallback shown. Set them to change the value.

A warmer, rounder card:

.hrefc-popup {
  --hrefc-bg: #fffdf7;
  --hrefc-radius: 18px;
  --hrefc-shadow: 0 10px 40px rgba(120, 80, 0, 0.18);
  --hrefc-desc: #6b5b3e;
}

docs.title: Level 2: classes
docs.text:
For anything the variables do not cover, write CSS against the classes. To change a box property such as padding or width directly, target .hrefc-card, the visible box. .hrefc-popup only positions and fades.

Class Part .hrefc-popup Positioning and fade wrapper .hrefc-card Visible box .hrefc-arrow Connector arrow .hrefc-head Favicon and title row .hrefc-favicon Favicon image .hrefc-title Title .hrefc-desc Description .hrefc-cta Call-to-action footer .hrefc-thumb Thumbnail image .hrefc-thumb-wide, .hrefc-thumb-half, .hrefc-thumb-float Thumbnail layout by aspect ratio (see Thumbnails) .hrefc-thumb-frame Wrapper for the iframe fallback 
.hrefc-title {
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
  text-decoration: underline;
  text-underline-offset: 3px;
}
.hrefc-favicon {
  border-radius: 50%;
}

docs.title: Style the call-to-action
docs.text:
Set content.cta and it renders as .hrefc-cta below the description:

.hrefc-cta {
  font-weight: 600;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  color: #2563eb;
}

Tip

To ship your own stylesheet instead of the injected one, set popup: { injectStyles: false }, then start from the standalone file: import 'vexy-hrefc/css', or copy dist/hrefc.css. The standalone file is built with the default prefix hrefc.

docs.title: Level 3: render()
docs.text:
When the structure itself must change, pass a render function. Its result replaces the default contents of .hrefc-card. The popup wrapper, the arrow and positioning still apply.

hrefc({
  render: (data) => `
    <article class="my-card">
      <h4>${data.title}</h4>
      <p>${data.description}</p>
    </article>
  `,
});

Warning

A returned string is set as innerHTML. Escape anything you do not control. There is a worked example in demo 05.

docs.title: Dark mode
docs.text:
By default the card follows the system setting through @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark). No configuration is needed.

To pin a palette, set popup.theme. It writes a data-theme attribute on .hrefc-popup:

hrefc({ popup: { theme: 'dark' } });   // always dark
hrefc({ popup: { theme: 'light' } });  // always light
hrefc({ popup: { theme: 'auto' } });   // follow the system (default)

To use your own dark palette, override the variables under the attribute:

.hrefc-popup[data-theme="dark"] {
  --hrefc-bg: #0d1117;
  --hrefc-fg: #e6edf3;
}

Users who set "reduce motion" in their system get a plain opacity fade without the upward slide.

docs.title: Font inheritance
docs.text: With popup.inheritFont: true (the default), the card uses font-family: inherit, so it reads as part of your page. Set it to false to use the system UI stack system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif instead.

docs.title: Rename classes
docs.text:
Change the prefix of every class with popup.classPrefix. The injected stylesheet uses the same prefix:

hrefc({ popup: { classPrefix: 'lp' } });
// .lp-popup, .lp-card, .lp-title, .lp-desc, …

Or rename single parts with the classes map. The default stylesheet does not follow these names, so style them yourself:

hrefc({ classes: { title: 'card__title', desc: 'card__body' } });

docs.title: Thumbnails
docs.text:
A card can show a picture of the target page as well as text. Thumbnails are off by default because text-only cards are smaller and need fewer requests. Switch them on with:

hrefc({ content: { thumbnail: true } });

With thumbnails on, the extractor also reads the page's image meta tags, and the card tries to show an image from a chain of providers.

docs.title: The provider chain
docs.text:
vexy-hrefc walks thumbnail.providers in order and uses the first provider that returns an image URL. The default chain is:

  1. ogimage: the image already extracted from the page, taken from the first non-empty og:image, og:image:url, twitter:image or twitter:image:src meta tag. It costs no extra request to find.
  2. mshots: a WordPress mShots screenshot, https://s0.wp.com/mshots/v1/<encoded url>?w=<thumbnail.width>. No key required.
  3. microlink: a Microlink screenshot, https://api.microlink.io/?url=<encoded url>&screenshot=true&embed=screenshot.url. Uses the keyless free tier.

The chain picks a URL without loading it. mshots and microlink always return a URL, so with the default chain a page without an Open Graph image gets an mshots screenshot.

After the URL is chosen:

  • If the image loads, it is laid out by its shape (see below).
  • If the image fails to load and thumbnail.iframe is true, the image is removed and the page itself is shown in a scaled iframe.
  • If no provider returned a URL and thumbnail.iframe is true, the iframe is used directly.
  • Otherwise the card shows text only. No broken-image icon appears.
hrefc({
  content: { thumbnail: true },
  thumbnail: {
    width: 480,
    providers: ['ogimage', 'mshots', 'microlink'],
    iframe: true,
    iframeViewport: { width: 1280, height: 800 },
  },
});

To use screenshots only and ignore Open Graph images, leave ogimage out of the chain:

hrefc({
  content: { thumbnail: true },
  thumbnail: { providers: ['mshots', 'microlink'] },
});

docs.title: The iframe fallback
docs.text:
The fallback renders the target page in an <iframe> at thumbnail.iframeViewport size (1280 × 800 by default), then scales it down with a CSS transform to the card's width. A desktop-size viewport keeps responsive sites from switching to their phone layout.

The iframe is created with sandbox="allow-same-origin" (so the page's scripts do not run), scrolling="no", loading="lazy", aria-hidden="true" and tabindex="-1". Sites that forbid framing (through X-Frame-Options or a CSP frame-ancestors rule) show a blank frame. Set thumbnail.iframe: false to skip the fallback.

docs.title: Layout by shape
docs.text:
The image is hidden until it loads. Then its natural aspect ratio (width ÷ height) picks a layout class:

Ratio Typical image Class Layout 1.25 (5:4) or wider Screenshots, social cards .hrefc-thumb-wide Full width, above the title Between 2:3 and 5:4 Square-ish images .hrefc-thumb-half 50% width, floated right 0.667 (2:3) or narrower Portraits, posters .hrefc-thumb-float 33% width, floated right

Text wraps beside floated images. Override any of these classes to change the layout.

docs.title: Custom providers
docs.text:
A provider is a function (url, data, opts) => string | null. It receives the page URL, the extracted data and the resolved thumbnail options. Return an image URL to use it, or null to pass to the next provider.

function myShot(url) {
  return 'https://my-screenshots.example/?url=' + encodeURIComponent(url);
}

hrefc({
  content: { thumbnail: true },
  thumbnail: { providers: ['ogimage', myShot] },
});

docs.title: Paid screenshot APIs
docs.text:
The keyless services suit low traffic. For faster and more reliable screenshots, use a paid screenshot API with your own key. The provider just builds the URL that service documents:

const KEY = '...'; // your key
function paidShot(url, _data, opts) {
  return 'https://api.example-screenshots.com/take'
    + '?access_key=' + KEY
    + '&url=' + encodeURIComponent(url)
    + '&viewport_width=' + (opts.width || 480);
}

hrefc({
  content: { thumbnail: true },
  thumbnail: { providers: ['ogimage', paidShot] },
});

The host and parameter names above are placeholders; use the ones your provider documents. Keys used in browser code are visible to anyone who reads the page source.

Note

The title and description appear as soon as the HTML is parsed. The image loads after that, and the card re-positions itself once the image size is known.

docs.title: Favicons
docs.text:
A favicon is a small site icon shown before the title, separate from the thumbnail. Enable it with:

hrefc({ content: { favicon: true } });

The extractor looks at every <link> whose rel contains icon and picks the one with the largest sizes value. If the page declares no icon, it uses /favicon.ico on the target's origin. If the favicon image fails to load, it is removed from the card.

Favicons and thumbnails are independent options; use either, both or neither.
